source.title: Approaching Deep Learning through the Spectral Dynamics of Weights
source.authors: David Yunis; Kumar Kshitij Patel; Samuel Wheeler; P. Savarese; Gal Vardi; Karen Livescu; Michael Maire; Matthew R. Walter

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes spectral properties in a new way and trains networks on true versus random CIFAR-10 labels, reporting differences in effective rank and inter-layer alignment. It does not report held-out accuracy for that comparison.
record.gate_note: The random-label experiment tests a spectral correlate of generalization versus memorization, not whether random-label memorization coexists with natural-label test accuracy. Rows cover the paper’s own true-versus-random-label rank and alignment measurements. Other spectral-dynamics and pruning results do not measure a version’s named behavior. The paper’s statements about validation loss and grokking concern a synthetic modular-addition task and do not bear on these versions.
record.test_reason: Section 6 explicitly reports zero training error for both true and random CIFAR-10 labels using the same MLP recipe. This tests V1's memorization-capacity component using the original random-label method. The extracted spectral measurements do not test V1, and the supplied text does not establish its held-out accuracy components.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately describes the authors' spectral conclusion: true-label and random-label solutions differ in rank and alignment. Add that both conditions achieve zero training error. The authors present these differences as a promising perspective on generalization, without establishing a comprehensive theory.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a 4-layer CIFAR-10 MLP and constant learning rate to compare true and random labels, focusing on spectral measurements rather than reproducing the original held-out accuracy results.
record.method_sensitivity: Label condition changes the measured rank and the persistence of inter-layer alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: True-label training produces lower-rank middle layers and persistent inter-layer alignment; random-label training produces higher rank and alignment that later disappears.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: True- and random-label fitting can differ in weight rank and inter-layer alignment despite both reaching zero training error.

record.problems: Only 3 random seeds per experiment. The random-label comparison does not report held-out accuracy, so it cannot establish the version’s memorization-and-generalization coexistence claim.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for this claim were included. Other paper experiments measure spectral dynamics, pruning, or linear mode connectivity rather than behaviors named by the listed versions.

untested.parts: Natural-label held-out accuracy far above chance and random-label held-out accuracy at chance cannot be established from the supplied text. Figure 8 includes validation-error panels, but their plotted values are unavailable in this text rendering.

missing.what: Extract the true-label and random-label validation-error results from Figure 8(b), including their relation to chance. The supplied text contains panel headings but no readable values, so the record's categorical assertion that held-out performance is not reported is unwarranted.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope verdict: measuring a different construct or leaving held-out components unresolved does not demonstrate a limitation of V1. Perturbation experiments concern linear mode connectivity, not V7's sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

versions.untested_parts: The study compares spectral properties for true and random CIFAR-10 labels, but does not report held-out accuracy or show that the same recipes fit both labelings.
